hero.headline: West Palm Beach soccer fan to cheer Cape Verde at World Cup in Miami
hero.body:
Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach is traveling to Miami this month to support Cape Verde as the island nation competes in the World Cup for the first time ever. Dacruz grew up on Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands off the African coast, before relocating to the United States. The nation, which gained independence from Portugal in the 1970s, has a population of only half a million people. Despite its small size, Cape Verde has qualified for one of the world's largest sporting events, making it among the smallest countries ever to reach the tournament.

The achievement has sparked tremendous excitement throughout Cape Verde. The national team, known as the Tubarão Azul or Blue Sharks, has captured the nation's attention in ways few things have before. Dacruz, who still has family members living in Cape Verde, said the qualification has been the dominant topic of conversation on the islands. "We're there you know. All we have to do is win a couple of games and we'll get far," Dacruz said, expressing confidence in his team's ability to advance. For Dacruz personally, attending a match will fulfill a lifelong dream. His girlfriend surprised him with tickets to Cape Verde's game against Uruguay in Miami as an anniversary gift. "It was our anniversary dinner and she gave me a little box with a handwritten note that said 'I'm going to the World Cup.' Didn't believe her at first, but an amazing gift," Dacruz said.

Cape Verde will open the tournament against Spain, one of the competition's favorites. The World Cup qualification brings significant benefits beyond national pride. The island nation's soccer federation will receive over 10 million dollars to invest in developing future generations of players. This financial boost represents a major opportunity for soccer development in the country. Dacruz is preparing for the match by waiting for his new Cape Verde national jersey to arrive in time for the game.

The archipelago has gained attention in other contexts as well. During hurricane season, weather forecasters frequently reference Cape Verde as tropical systems form near the islands before potentially tracking westward across the Atlantic toward the United States. The region's geography makes it a key point in Atlantic weather patterns that meteorologists monitor throughout the hurricane season. For Dacruz and countless other Cape Verdeans, however, the focus this month remains on soccer and the historic opportunity for their small nation to compete on the world's biggest sports stage.

cards.headline: 2-year-old drowns in Fort Pierce swimming pool after leaving home unnoticed
cards.body:
A 2-year-old child drowned in Fort Pierce over the weekend after being discovered unresponsive in a swimming pool. The incident took place at a residence in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue on Saturday. According to police, the child managed to unlock a door and exit the home while family members were inside, going unnoticed during this time.

When family members realized the child was missing, they searched the property and found the child already in the swimming pool and unresponsive. They immediately began providing first aid to the child before Fort Pierce police officers arrived at the scene. Officers continued life-saving efforts, and the child was transported to a local hospital for emergency treatment.

Despite receiving medical care, the child's condition was critical, and police said the child ultimately died from the injuries sustained. The investigation into the drowning remains ongoing as authorities work to document the circumstances surrounding this tragedy.

This incident represents another young child's death by drowning in the area. A 2-year-old drowned in a Greenacres canal in March, and another 2-year-old drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May, highlighting a concerning pattern of drowning deaths among young children in the region.

cards.headline: 6.1 Magnitude Earthquake Off Cuba Shakes Buildings Across Florida
cards.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Cuba on Monday afternoon, triggering widespread reports of shaking throughout Florida. The U.S. Geological Survey confirmed the earthquake occurred just after 2 p.m., approximately 65 miles west of Mantua, Cuba, at a depth of roughly 10 miles below the surface. The shallow depth of the quake allowed the tremors to travel across the water and be felt across much of the state, from the Tampa Bay area down to Miami-Dade County, creating an unusual seismic experience for residents unaccustomed to earthquake activity.

Residents across South Florida quickly shared their experiences on social media, describing the shaking they felt in various locations. Carol Carsten in Port Saint Lucie reported feeling "just the slightest of shaking" while lying on a chaise lounge in her lanai. A viewer in Fort Pierce on the fifth floor noted they could "actually feel the floor swaying." Lynn Wollman in Boynton Beach said "our whole building was swaying for a good 5-7 seconds," while Erica Smith Chepurko in North Palm Beach described how "my TV and computer monitor shook" on the fourth floor of her office building. Near Tampa, residents reported feeling their patio furniture shake and expressed surprise at the unusual phenomenon.

In response to the earthquake, authorities took precautionary measures as the seismic activity prompted building evacuations. The Miami-Dade Government Center and Miami Beach City Hall were evacuated out of an abundance of caution. The National Weather Service in Miami confirmed receiving reports of shaking from across southwestern Florida. Officials quickly worked to reassure the public about tsunami concerns, with the National Tsunami Warning Center announcing there was "no tsunami danger for the U.S. east coast, the Gulf of America states, or the eastern coast of Canada."

Authorities continue to monitor the situation following the quake. No aftershocks have been reported since the initial earthquake, and no damage has been documented in Florida. While the state has no documented active fault lines, seismic activity originating in Cuba and the Caribbean region can occasionally be felt across South Florida due to its proximity to active fault zones. This earthquake, though significant and unusual for the area, caused no injuries or significant damage in either Florida or Cuba, where the quake was also felt in Havana.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach man arrested in fatal shooting of Plantation father in Boca Raton parking lot
cards.teaser: Willie Byrd Jr., a 42-year-old Boynton Beach man, has been arrested in the fatal shooting of a Plantation father who was gunned down in a Boca Raton parking lot in April.
cards.body:
A 42-year-old Boynton Beach man has been arrested and charged with first-degree murder with a firearm in the fatal shooting of 37-year-old Arman Motiwalla, a Plantation father. Willie Byrd Jr. was taken into custody Friday and is being held at Palm Beach County Jail. Motiwalla was discovered with multiple gunshot wounds next to his car around 1:45 a.m. on April 8 in the parking lot of 350 Camino Gardens Boulevard in Boca Raton. According to a probable cause affidavit, surveillance footage captured the shooting on the evening of April 7, and Motiwalla's Apple Watch recorded his last heartbeat at 8:25 p.m.

The investigation revealed Byrd drove a silver Chrysler 200 with stolen license plates to conceal the vehicle's identity. Surveillance data and license-plate readers tracked Byrd from his Boynton Beach residence to the Boca Raton crime scene and back home. A search warrant on Byrd's vehicle uncovered a Post-It note containing the Camino Gardens address, Motiwalla's name, personal address and fiancée's name, along with 9mm magazines, ammunition, Western Union receipts and Chase Bank account information. Cell phone data analysis revealed Byrd had surveilled Motiwalla's workplace. Motiwalla had filed a whistleblower complaint against his former employer, Innovative Partners L.P., in 2025.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove named one of America's fastest-growing neighborhoods
cards.body:
RentCafe has recognized Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code as one of the fastest-growing in the country, a distinction driven primarily by the rapid expansion of Southern Grove. The neighborhood, which was virtually nonexistent a decade ago, has experienced remarkable transformation with housing inventory surging by 177 percent, marking one of Florida's most significant growth periods. This explosive development reflects a deliberate urban planning strategy designed to attract and retain residents in the area.

The neighborhood's appeal stems largely from its emergence as a major employment center. Major corporations including FedEx and Amazon have established operations in Southern Grove, with Amazon demonstrating particular commitment by closing its existing facility this year to construct a significantly larger replacement. Beyond employment opportunities, the area has gained recognition for its educated population and elevated homeownership rates, creating a stable community foundation. Southern Grove represents one of four intentionally designed neighborhoods in Port St. Lucie meant to provide residents with compelling reasons to relocate to and remain in the community.

Florida's prominence in growth rankings reflects broader economic factors that have made the state increasingly attractive to businesses and residents. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida ranks second only to Texas among states with the most up-and-coming communities. The state's favorable tax climate and housing costs that remain relatively affordable compared to major metropolitan areas like New York and California have fueled this expansion. Ongoing infrastructure investments have complemented these advantages, spurring construction activity throughout numerous growing suburban areas.

Port St. Lucie is not alone in gaining national recognition. Ponte Vedra Beach earned the top position on RentCafe's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list, appealing to families, retirees, and young professionals through its distinctive character. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine region also secured spots in the top 50, drawing attention for their strong schools and robust housing demand. These communities demonstrate Florida's broader trajectory as an increasingly desirable destination for people seeking new opportunities and improved quality of life.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Golf Club $30 million renovation 50 percent complete, set to finish by end of 2026
cards.teaser: Delray Beach Golf Club's massive renovation is making impressive progress, with the project already 50 percent complete as of early June.
cards.body:
The Delray Beach Golf Club's $30 million renovation is 50 percent complete as of early June, with city officials on track to finish by the end of 2026. The course has been closed since November 2025 for the makeover, which aims to restore its historic character while providing modern upgrades. Ronnie Dunayer, a golf instructor who has taught at the course for 20 years, recently got a sneak peek at the progress and said it exceeded her expectations. "I've been an advocate for improvement for a long time, and in all honesty, it's looking better than anticipated," Dunayer said. She noted the renovation preserves the old integrity of the course while making improvements, though she acknowledged some changes to bunkers will make play more difficult.

The renovation is happening in phases, with the north 9 holes, called the Wilson 9, already fully grassed and growing in. The south 9 holes, the Ross 9, are currently being grassed. The original course was designed by legendary architects Donald Ross and Dick Wilson, and the city is working to preserve those historic elements. However, not all residents support the changes. Delray Beach resident Maureen Allyn expressed concerns about large planting holes for trees near her home that could block her view of the golf course and potentially impact her property's value. The city says the $30 million budget has not changed since work began, and they are still targeting a November 2026 reopening date.

cards.headline: Brightline and Tri-Rail offer transit options to Hard Rock Stadium for World Cup matches in Miami
cards.teaser: Thousands of fans heading to Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens for the 2026 FIFA World Cup can save significant money compared to driving and parking by using Brightline or Tri-Rail.
cards.body:
Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens will host seven FIFA World Cup 2026 matches, beginning Monday, June 15, when Saudi Arabia plays Uruguay at 6 p.m. The final Miami match, the third-place playoff, is scheduled for Saturday, July 18 at 5 p.m. Brightline is the official transit partner, offering round-trip tickets ranging from $76 to $150. From the Brightline Aventura Station, the closest designated transit hub to the stadium, Miami-Dade County will provide free Game Day Express shuttle buses directly to stadium gates on a first-come, first-served basis for passengers with valid World Cup match tickets.

Tri-Rail provides a more affordable option with one-way tickets from $2.50 to $6.90 depending on the starting station, and weekend round-trip travel available for $5. Both transit services cost less than driving, as Hard Rock Stadium parking passes require advance purchase with some costing up to $200. Additional transit options include Metrorail or Tri-Rail to the Miami-Dade Golden Glades Interchange with a connection via Metrobus Route 297 (Orange Express), or rideshare services like Uber and Lyft at designated zones, though surge pricing and longer wait times are expected after matches. Fans are encouraged to check the official FIFA World Cup Miami website for updated transit and shuttle information.

cards.headline: Jupiter boaters rescue 324-pound sea turtle in distress near Jupiter Sound
cards.teaser: Four friends boating in Jupiter Sound rescued a 324-pound adult female sea turtle that had been struck by a boat, though the turtle died hours later.
cards.body:
Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony were boating in Jupiter Sound when they noticed a 324-pound adult female sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway, clearly injured and in need of help. Working together, the four men carefully tied a rope around the turtle's shell and guided her toward Blowing Rocks Marina. Once they got the turtle, which they named Zoey, out of the water, her shell was covered in deep cuts, and her head drooped weakly, telltale signs she had been struck by a boat.

The Loggerhead Marinelife Center responded quickly to the marina, confirming that Zoey had indeed suffered severe injuries from a boat strike. Despite the team's heroic efforts and the marine center's care, Zoey passed away just hours later. NOAA estimates that hundreds to thousands of sea turtles are struck by vessels in the U.S. every year, and many of them are killed. In Florida alone, injuries consistent with vessel strikes are observed in 20 to 30 percent of stranded sea turtles. Adult sea turtles are particularly vulnerable to vessel strikes during nesting season, which runs in Florida from March through October.

cards.headline: Pride on the Block raises funds for Transpire Help as government cuts reduce services
cards.teaser: The event at The Peach in West Palm Beach serves as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, which provides substance use treatment, mental health care and housing to LGBTQ+ individuals.
cards.body:
Pride on the Block brought together neighbors, allies and activists at The Peach in West Palm Beach on Saturday to support the LGBTQ+ community. The event served as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a nonprofit that provides substance use treatment, mental health care and stable housing to LGBTQ+ individuals.

Donna Weinberger, founder of Transpire Help, said the fundraiser is more important than ever as cuts to government funding have slashed the number of people the organization can help in half. Weinberger noted that a significant part of the community, especially gender diverse people, lack health insurance or funds and would be unable to access treatment otherwise. Performer Liam Chambers credited Transpire Help with helping turn his life around. Chambers said he is three years sober and now performs as a drag king, which he would not have been able to do without the organization's support.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie 9-year-old launches junior chess club to share his love of the game
cards.teaser: Orion Jean Baptiste started the club to help kids learn about chess and develop focus, patience and strategic thinking skills.
cards.body:
A new juniors chess club has launched in Port St. Lucie, inspired by 9-year-old Orion Jean Baptiste who wanted to share his love of the game with his community. Baptiste's passion for chess began at age 5, playing alongside family members. Now he hopes to pass that passion on to others. "I just wanted kids to learn about chess," Baptiste said. He also expressed concern about society's focus on technology, saying "Everybody's more focused on like tech stuff. I'm hoping that more people have respect for board games."

Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, said chess will help develop the next generation of leaders. "[It] will help to build leaders or members that are more focused, more patient, more strategic and thoughtful in their decision [making]," Kempton said. The Atlantis Chess Club has already attracted more than 36 juniors at the Port St. Lucie location and meets every Friday. The club will soon begin two additional programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce. Thomas Furlong, a father who brought his children to the club, praised the setting as ideal for his family to learn and compete together. His daughter Francesca, one of the club's newest members, said the best part is "playing with other kids."

"It was our anniversary dinner and she gave me a little box with a handwritten note that said 'I'm going to the World Cup.' Didn't believe her at first, but an amazing gift," Dacruz said.

Cape Verde will open the tournament against Spain, one of the competition's favorites. The World Cup qualification brings significant benefits beyond national pride. The island nation's soccer federation will receive over 10 million dollars to invest in developing future generations of players. This financial boost represents a major opportunity for soccer development in the country. Dacruz is preparing for the match by waiting for his new Cape Verde national jersey to arrive in time for the game.

The archipelago has gained attention in other contexts as well. During hurricane season, weather forecasters frequently reference Cape Verde as tropical systems form near the islands before potentially tracking westward across the Atlantic toward the United States. The region's geography makes it a key point in Atlantic weather patterns that meteorologists monitor throughout the hurricane season. For Dacruz and countless other Cape Verdeans, however, the focus this month remains on soccer and the historic opportunity for their small nation to compete on the world's biggest sports stage.

cards.headline: Four men rescue 324-pound injured sea turtle in Jupiter Sound
cards.teaser: Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony rescued a badly injured green sea turtle in Jupiter Sound after spotting her struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
Four friends enjoying a day on the water near Jupiter became heroes when they spotted a massive green sea turtle in distress. Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony were boating in Jupiter Sound when they noticed something wasn't right. A 324-pound adult female sea turtle was struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway, clearly injured and in need of help. Working together, the four men carefully tied a rope around the turtle's shell and guided her toward Blowing Rocks Marina. Once they got the turtle, which they named Zoey, out of the water, her shell was covered in deep cuts, and her head drooped weakly, telltale signs she'd been struck by a boat.

The Loggerhead Marinelife Center responded quickly to the marina, confirming that Zoey had indeed suffered severe injuries from a boat strike. Despite the team's heroic efforts and the marine center's care, Zoey passed away just hours later. According to NOAA, hundreds to thousands of sea turtles are struck by vessels in the U.S. every year, and many of them are killed. In Florida alone, injuries consistent with vessel strikes are observed in 20 to 30 percent of stranded sea turtles. Adult sea turtles are particularly vulnerable to vessel strikes during nesting season, which runs in Florida from March through October.

cards.teaser: RentCafe named Port St. Lucie's 34987 one of the fastest-growing zip codes in the country, thanks to Southern Grove, which has seen housing inventory explode by 177%.

hero.headline: 'Beetlejuice' the musical playing at West Palm Beach's Kravis Center through June 7
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit brings spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall at the Kravis Center, with performances running through Saturday.
hero.body:
From wigs gone rogue to audience laughter echoing through the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall, 'Beetlejuice' the musical has landed at the Kravis Center. Running June 2 through June 7, the Broadway hit brings its spooky humor, over-the-top visuals, and heartwarming moments to Palm Beach County. Actor Ryan Stajmiger steps into the iconic striped suit to play the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen, whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble.

Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. He gets to break the fourth wall and communicate directly to the audience and share moments with them. Very early in the run, he experienced an unexpected moment when his wig change went wrong. He was wearing two wigs, and the second wig came off with the first wig, so he was bald for an entire scene and got to play with that a little bit.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50, and the safest and most secure way to get them is to buy directly at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach to host 80-mile ocean paddle for Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the Atlantic Ocean this June in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. The event launches from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13, with participants expected to arrive at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. Event founder Travis Suit established the fundraiser to benefit the Piper's Angels Foundation, which he created in honor of his daughter, Piper, who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4.

The four-day event begins June 10 with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. Thursday includes a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner, while Friday features a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by safety checks before the midnight launch. All paddlers must wear a U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device, waterproof whistle, and reflective gear during dark hours, along with GPS trackers that must remain active throughout the crossing. Participants must raise a minimum of $2,000, with crew and virtual participants requiring $500. Final contributions are due by July 31. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to celebrate the paddlers' arrival. For registration and donations, visit crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

hero.headline: 6.1 Magnitude Earthquake Off Cuba Shakes Buildings Across Florida
hero.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Cuba on Monday afternoon, triggering widespread reports of shaking throughout Florida. The U.S. Geological Survey confirmed the earthquake occurred just after 2 p.m., approximately 65 miles west of Mantua, Cuba, at a depth of roughly 10 miles below the surface. The shallow depth of the quake allowed the tremors to travel across the water and be felt across much of the state, from the Tampa Bay area down to Miami-Dade County, creating an unusual seismic experience for residents unaccustomed to earthquake activity.

Residents across South Florida quickly shared their experiences on social media, describing the shaking they felt in various locations. Carol Carsten in Port Saint Lucie reported feeling "just the slightest of shaking" while lying on a chaise lounge in her lanai. A viewer in Fort Pierce on the fifth floor noted they could "actually feel the floor swaying." Lynn Wollman in Boynton Beach said "our whole building was swaying for a good 5-7 seconds," while Erica Smith Chepurko in North Palm Beach described how "my TV and computer monitor shook" on the fourth floor of her office building. Near Tampa, residents reported feeling their patio furniture shake and expressed surprise at the unusual phenomenon.

In response to the earthquake, authorities took precautionary measures as the seismic activity prompted building evacuations. The Miami-Dade Government Center and Miami Beach City Hall were evacuated out of an abundance of caution. The National Weather Service in Miami confirmed receiving reports of shaking from across southwestern Florida. Officials quickly worked to reassure the public about tsunami concerns, with the National Tsunami Warning Center announcing there was "no tsunami danger for the U.S. east coast, the Gulf of America states, or the eastern coast of Canada."

Authorities continue to monitor the situation following the quake. No aftershocks have been reported since the initial earthquake, and no damage has been documented in Florida. While the state has no documented active fault lines, seismic activity originating in Cuba and the Caribbean region can occasionally be felt across South Florida due to its proximity to active fault zones. This earthquake, though significant and unusual for the area, caused no injuries or significant damage in either Florida or Cuba, where the quake was also felt in Havana.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Rep. Debra Tendrich Named Florida Elected Official of Year by Social Workers
cards.teaser: The freshman lawmaker who sponsored landmark domestic violence legislation this session received the honor from the Florida Chapter of the National Association of Social Workers.
cards.body:
Lake Worth Democratic Rep. Debra Tendrich has been named the 2026 Florida Elected Official of the Year by the Florida Chapter of the National Association of Social Workers, which represents some 3,000 professional social workers statewide. The award recognizes public officials whose work demonstrates leadership in human services and dedication to serving the community. She will be formally recognized at the organization's annual conference awards luncheon on June 12 in Orlando. The recognition caps Tendrich's first term, largely defined by her work as a domestic violence survivor-turned-legislative champion.

Her signature legislation this past session, HB 277, passed unanimously in both chambers and was signed last month by Gov. Ron DeSantis. The bill strengthens protections for survivors, enhances penalties for repeat offenders, increases victim relocation assistance and establishes a GPS monitoring pilot program. Tendrich, who fled her abuser in 2012 with her daughter, has described the bill as turning "pain into policy." The nomination also cited her Eat Better Live Better nonprofit, which focused on combating food insecurity and childhood obesity through healthy food access and nutrition education, and her service on the Florida Atlantic University School of Social Work Advisory Board. Tendrich represents House District 89 in Palm Beach County and is running for re-election unopposed.

cards.headline: FAU Economists Warn Summer Vacations Will Be More Expensive This Year
cards.teaser: Florida Atlantic University economists project inflation will remain above the Federal Reserve's target of 2%, with rising costs for food services, accommodations and recreation.
cards.body:
Florida Atlantic University economists warn that summer vacations will cost more as travelers head into the coming months. The FAU analysis concludes elevated inflation will lead to increasingly expensive summer trips, with the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index's annual growth of inflation climbing to 4.9% in April. Economists project inflation will remain above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. "For households planning summer vacations, this is not good news," said Eric Van Tassel, Associate Professor of Economics in FAU's College of Business. Van Tassel identified some of the fastest-growing price categories as food services and accommodations, housing and utilities, as well as recreation services. He added that inflation grew at an annualized rate of 3.8% over the last six months and 3.3% over the last year.

Associate Professor William Luther attributed the challenging economic environment to President Donald Trump's application of international tariffs and the war with Iran. Luther noted that nominal spending actually grew 5.9% in the first quarter of this year compared to the first quarter of 2025. The economists concluded inflation has likely peaked, but it will take time before prices moderate. Heads of households will be making spending decisions this summer while lodging, dining and recreational costs likely will remain high at least until fall.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds Says He's Not Concerned About Ron DeSantis Cold Shoulder
cards.teaser: The Naples congressman running for governor said he's not worried about the current governor's criticism, noting Florida has term limits and DeSantis' time is ending.
cards.body:
Ron DeSantis has yet to walk back criticisms of Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds, but the Naples congressman said Monday on HotCakes and Hot Takes that he is not concerned about it. Donalds noted that Florida has term limits and DeSantis' time is coming to a close. DeSantis said earlier this year that Donalds has not been part of any victories achieved over the left in recent years, a statement that continues to circulate as the governor has refused to endorse a potential successor. Donalds said DeSantis was still aggrieved that he endorsed Donald Trump over the governor in the 2024 presidential race. "I'm not going to get mad about it," Donalds said. "He's done a great job for the state. We're going to have a new Governor in six months and a week."

Despite DeSantis' criticism of Donalds' record, the third-term congressman and former state legislator is confident enough in his chances for the nomination that he would not name an opponent he saw as a threat. Donalds said other candidates are polling in single digits while his polling shows him at 50% or slightly higher. "It's a winner-take-all state. It's not even 50 plus one, it's the most votes," Donalds said. With two and a half months remaining before the election, he said the campaign takes nothing for granted.

cards.headline: Florida's History of Feeling Distant Earthquakes
cards.teaser: Monday's 6.1 earthquake off Cuba is not the first time Florida residents have felt ground shake because of seismic events hundreds of miles away.
cards.body:
Despite there being no documented active fault lines in Florida, the state has a history of residents feeling earthquakes from distant locations. In February 2024, residents across the Treasure Coast felt the ground shake after a 4.0 magnitude earthquake hit off Florida's east coast about 100 miles east of Cape Canaveral in the Atlantic Ocean. In January 2020, residents in Miami felt the ground shake from a 7.7 earthquake that hit off the coast of Jamaica. That quake was centered 86 miles northwest of Montego Bay, Jamaica, and 87 miles west-southwest of Niquero, Cuba, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

According to the Florida Division of Emergency Management, seismic activity is rare in Florida, and no earthquakes have had an epicenter in Florida because there are no documented active faults in the state. Shaking felt in Florida comes from earthquakes either in the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean, or from the small fault line northeast of the state near Charleston, South Carolina. According to USGS, Florida is classified as a stable geological area, which means that damage from any shaking or tremors felt from an earthquake is expected to be minimal.

cards.headline: Venice Mayor Nick Pachota Raises Nearly $379,000 for House District 74 Bid
cards.teaser: The Republican candidate announced his campaign has raised just over $243,500 through his official campaign account, with another $135,000 raised through his political committee.
cards.body:

The campaign announced support from multiple first responder organizations, including the Suncoast Professional Firefighters and Paramedics, the Florida Professional Firefighters, the Florida Police Benevolent Association, the National Association of Police Organizations, the International Union of Police Associations, and Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 57. These endorsements add to previous support from Sarasota Sheriff Kurt Hoffman, the Sarasota Area Medical PAC, and Rep. James Buchanan, the term-limited incumbent who endorsed Pachota as his successor.

The race to succeed Buchanan has drawn multiple well-funded candidates. Kelly Ann Walker, endorsed by Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson, reported approximately $258,000 in cash on hand across her campaign and political committee. Jennifer Winkler, a Sarasota business owner, has raised $150,000. The Republican field also includes Chris Felder and Les Nichols. The GOP Primary is scheduled for August 18, with the General Election in November. Buchanan has represented HD 74 since 2018 and is running for Senate District 22.

cards.headline: Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava Endorses Ashley Gantt for Senate District 34
cards.teaser: Miami-Dade County's top local official joined seven sitting Senate Democrats who announced their support for the Miami representative last week.
cards.body:
Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava endorsed Miami Democratic Rep. Ashley Gantt's bid for Senate District 34 this week, joining seven sitting Senate Democrats in backing her candidacy. Levine Cava, Miami-Dade's first woman and Jewish mayor, said in a statement that "Ashley Gantt stands out as one of the most dedicated, effective, and passionate advocates our region has ever produced." She added that Miami-Dade needs a State Senator who will fight for the county's fair share of resources and stand up for its values in Tallahassee. Senate Democratic Leader Lori Berman and Sens. Mack Bernard, LaVon Bracy Davis, Carlos Guillermo Smith, Rosalind Osgood, Tina Scott Polsky and Barbara Sharief also back Gantt.

Gantt, a lawyer and former public school teacher who serves as president of the T.J. Reddick Bar Association and Gwen S. Cherry Black Women Lawyers Association, launched her SD 34 campaign on May 29, shortly after Miami Gardens Democratic Sen. Shevrin Jones announced he would not seek re-election there. As of Monday when Levine Cava's endorsement was announced, Gantt was the only candidate in the race. SD 34 covers northeast Miami-Dade, including Bay Harbor Islands, Miami Beach, North Miami, North Miami Beach, Opa-locka and Miami Gardens. The Primary Election is scheduled for August 18, followed by the General Election in November.

According to a preliminary investigation, while family members were inside the residence, the child was able to unlock a door and leave the home unnoticed. When family members realized the child was missing, they began searching the property and discovered the child unresponsive in the swimming pool.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove neighborhood ranks among fastest-growing zip codes in America
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code has been named one of the fastest-growing in the country, with Southern Grove seeing housing inventory explode by 177 percent.
hero.body:
RentCafe has recognized Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code as one of the fastest-growing in the country, largely due to the rapid development of Southern Grove, a neighborhood that has transformed dramatically over the past decade. The area's housing inventory has surged by 177 percent, representing one of the most significant growth spurts across Florida. This expansion reflects both deliberate planning and strong market demand that has positioned Southern Grove as an increasingly attractive place to live and work.

The neighborhood's appeal extends beyond housing numbers. Southern Grove has emerged as a significant employment center, drawing major corporations to the area. FedEx and Amazon have established major operations here, with Amazon demonstrating particular commitment by planning to close its existing facility and construct a larger replacement facility later this year. The neighborhood has also gained recognition for maintaining educated residents and strong homeownership rates, factors that contribute to its overall quality of life.

The growth of Southern Grove was not random. The neighborhood was intentionally developed as one of four distinct communities designed to attract residents and encourage them to establish long-term roots in the area. This strategic planning approach has clearly paid dividends, as the community continues to expand and develop. Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, notes that Florida's success in attracting growth stems from multiple factors. "Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California," Both explained. She added that "sustained infrastructure investment has also fueled construction activity in many of these growing suburbs."

Port St. Lucie is not the only Florida community experiencing significant growth and recognition. Ponte Vedra Beach topped RentCafe's list of America's 50 newest neighborhoods, earning praise for creating an environment that appeals to families, retirees, and young professionals. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area have also achieved recognition in the top 50, noted for their excellent schools and robust housing demand. These communities demonstrate that Florida's growth extends well beyond individual zip codes, reflecting broader trends that are reshaping the state's landscape and attracting residents from across the country.

cards.headline: 42-year-old Boynton Beach man arrested in fatal shooting of Plantation father in Boca Raton
cards.teaser: Willie Byrd Jr. of Boynton Beach was arrested Friday and charged with first-degree murder in the April shooting death of 37-year-old Arman Motiwalla in a Boca Raton parking lot.
cards.body:
Willie Byrd Jr., 42, of Boynton Beach was arrested Friday and charged with first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of 37-year-old Arman Motiwalla, according to Boca Raton police. Byrd is being held at Palm Beach County Jail. Motiwalla was found with multiple gunshot wounds next to his car around 1:45 a.m. on April 8 in the parking lot of 350 Camino Gardens Boulevard in Boca Raton. Police had offered a $3,000 reward for information leading to an arrest.

According to a probable cause affidavit from the Boca Raton Police Department, surveillance footage captured the shooting on the evening of April 7, and Motiwalla's Apple Watch recorded his last heartbeat at 8:25 p.m. The investigation revealed Byrd drove a silver Chrysler 200 with stolen license plates. Surveillance data and license-plate readers tracked Byrd from his Boynton Beach residence to the crime scene and back home. A search warrant on Byrd's vehicle uncovered a Post-It note containing the Camino Gardens address, Motiwalla's name, personal address and his fiancée's name, along with 9mm magazines, ammunition, Western Union receipts and Chase Bank account information. Cell phone data analysis revealed Byrd had surveilled Motiwalla's workplace and coordinated with an associate. Motiwalla had filed a whistleblower complaint against his former employer, Innovative Partners L.P., in 2025.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Golf Club renovation 50% complete, on track for November reopening
cards.teaser: The $30 million renovation of Delray Beach Golf Club is halfway done and on schedule to reopen by the end of 2026, with the historic Donald Ross and Dick Wilson course design being preserved.
cards.body:
The Delray Beach Golf Club's $30 million renovation is 50 percent complete as of early June and remains on track for a November 2026 reopening. The course has been closed since November 2025 for the makeover, which aims to restore its historic character while providing modern upgrades. City officials have maintained the project budget and timeline since work began.

Ronnie Dunayer, a golf instructor who has taught at the course for 20 years, recently toured the renovation progress and said it exceeded her expectations. The original course was designed by legendary architects Donald Ross and Dick Wilson, and the city is preserving those historic elements. The renovation is happening in phases, with the north 9 holes, called the Wilson 9, already fully grassed and growing in, while the south 9 holes, the Ross 9, are currently being grassed. However, some residents have concerns. Delray Beach resident Maureen Allyn contacted WPTV about large planting holes for trees being opened near her home, worried the trees could block her view of the golf course and negatively impact her property's value.

cards.headline: Brightline and Tri-Rail offer transit options to World Cup matches at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami
cards.teaser: Thousands of fans heading to Hard Rock Stadium for the World Cup can save money by taking Brightline or Tri-Rail instead of driving and paying parking fees as high as $200.
cards.body:
Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens will host seven FIFA World Cup 2026 matches, beginning Monday, June 15, when Saudi Arabia plays Uruguay at 6 p.m. The final Miami match, the third-place match, is scheduled for Saturday, July 18 at 5 p.m. Brightline is the official transit partner for the tournament, offering round-trip tickets ranging from $76 to $150. From the Brightline Aventura Station, the designated transit hub closest to the stadium, Miami-Dade County will provide free Game Day Express shuttle buses directly to the stadium gates. Shuttles operate on a first-come, first-served basis, and riders must present a valid World Cup match ticket for that specific day to board.

Tri-Rail provides a more affordable option, with one-way tickets ranging from $2.50 to $6.90 depending on the starting station, and weekend round-trip travel available for $5. Both transit options are cheaper than driving, as parking passes for Hard Rock Stadium must be purchased in advance, with some costing as much as $200. Additional transportation alternatives include Metrorail or Metrobus via Route 297 (Orange Express) from the Miami-Dade Golden Glades Interchange, or rideshare services like Uber and Lyft at designated zones, though surge pricing and longer wait times are expected following matches.
